_doc: MANUAL full-chain demo_video validation against a REAL interactive app (TodoMVC — the canonical Playwright demo SPA: add/complete/delete todos = real type/click interactions, fast & deterministic). example.com is a degenerate target (near-empty DOM → the generated BDD suite hangs on missing elements → FTR _run_tests 600s timeout); TodoMVC generates working, fast-completing scenarios so the record->compile->MP4 tail actually produces a video with real interactions. NO pause: runs gen -> narrate ∥ record -> compile -> growth_bundle. Asserts gen lines, record interaction clips w/ video_url, narration audio clips, and a non-empty compiled MP4 artifact_url. ⚠️ target_duration_seconds LOWERED 60 -> 30 on 2026-08-23, measured not guessed. On run 01a03011 this fixture ordered 60s from TodoMVC with two focus_areas: the derivation correctly asked bdd for ceil(60/4.0)=15 scenarios, bdd generated 5, capture returned all 5 (no shortfall), and the measured yield was 5.45s/beat — ABOVE the 4.0s assumed. 5 x 5.45 = 27.26s, so reconcile_timeline hard-failed at 45.4% of target, correctly. max_scenarios_per_feature is a CEILING, not a quota: a trivial app yields what it affords whatever ceiling it is given. Asking 60s of TodoMVC is unsatisfiable BY CONSTRUCTION — the same shape this fixture was supposed to have stopped demonstrating. 30s sits just above the 27.26s the app actually affords. ⚠️ RAISED 30 -> 44 on 2026-09-11 — ARITHMETIC, not tuning. bdd guarantees a fixed recording dwell per scenario (HERO_DWELL_MS, on the wire as narration_script.parts[].expected_recording_seconds), measured at 22.00s on live run 01a0b3f1. An N-scenario demo therefore has a HARD floor of N x 22.00s, and this fixture's own expect_stage_assertions demand distinct_count_gte(lines[].id) >= 2 — so its floor is 2 x 22.00 = 44.00s and a 30s order was UNREACHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: the run delivered 47.045s (+56.8%), then structural relief spawned a child that delivered 19.95s (-33.5%). Neither pass is inside duration_conformance's +/-10% band. 44s makes the order feasible (44.00s floor == 44.00s ordered; the 47.045s actually delivered is +6.9%, inside the band 39.60-48.40s). This is a FIXTURE correction — the order was unrealistic for the scenario count the fixture itself requires.

expect_stage_assertions._checks_doc: lines[].id floor RAISED 1 -> 2 on 2026-09-05. A 1-item floor cannot tell a real spine from a degenerate one-beat film, which is the same class of hole that let site_capture return `completed` with zero screens. 2 is MEASURED, not guessed: gen.py::_scenarios_for_target's own docstring records E2E run 01a03011 — THIS scenario, same TodoMVC target, same two focus_areas — generating FIVE scenarios, so the floor has 2.5x headroom. demo_video_calibration already uses 2. `features_generated` (DemoVideoGenOutput, gen.py:365) is added alongside: it is set from result.features_generated at gen.py:502 on the bdd path and is 0 only in authored mode (gen.py:440), which this scenario is not.

_pixel_doc:
bounds are FULL-RANGE [0,255], not broadcast-legal [16,235]: this is a web/computer screen recording (TodoMVC), so real footage legitimately contains pure-black text/letterbox (YMIN=0) and pure-white background (YMAX=255) — a broadcast-legal floor of 16 hard-fails every real master (verified: live compile YMIN=0, YAVG 235-255). Legal luma is unachievable pre-encode anyway (libx264 ringing). The real non-degenerate-video signal here is yavg_spread_max (no wild brightness swings) + min_frames (a substantial video, not a 1-frame stub); the upstream demo_video_record blank-gate (#654 sharpness) already rejects blank clips before compile.

⚠️ STAGE RE-BINDING 2026-09-11: every pixel check in this file used to be bound to `demo_video_compile`, so NOTHING in it ever probed the artifact this scenario actually DELIVERS. `demo_video_encode_master` is the delivered stage — it sits downstream of compile (src/services/blueprints/demo_video.py, depends_on=("demo_video_footage_critique",)) and runs the mastering critic/advisor loop, so the master's bytes are NOT the compile draft's bytes and a compile-bound assertion cannot refute a mastering regression. The four media ACCEPTANCE checks (artifact_reachable / audio_present / resolution / stream_durations) and `declared_vs_measured` are therefore bound to `demo_video_encode_master`, structurally copied from the sibling demo_video_full_chain.json with ITS floors — min_bytes 4096, >=1280x720 16:9, video>=10s, audio>=5s — deliberately NOT new tuning numbers invented for this fixture. `signalstats_delta` and `min_frames` STAY on `demo_video_compile`: they are legitimately pre-encode probes of the draft's pixels (and their full-range bounds above were measured on a compile output, not on a master). `duration_within_tolerance` is present and DISARMED (`"enabled": false`) carrying `ordered_seconds: 44` to match this fixture's own corrected order; arming it is out of scope here — no type has a measured tolerance band yet.

expect_pixel_checks._doc: Header-vs-packets guard on the delivered master. THE incident: an mp4 whose `moov` declared 12.0s over data that demuxed to 2.84s of picture. Every header-reading duration assertion reads that same claim -- in the recorded case `stream_durations` even saw a 0.00s A/V skew, because both numbers came from the one lying mux -- so a master whose picture stopped 9s early passed all of them. This is the only check that compares the DECLARED duration against the duration that actually demuxes (packet count / avg_frame_rate), which is what makes the disagreement visible. No thresholds are pinned here on purpose: the tolerance lives once, in scripts/e2e_validate.py.
